page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highmem-4 in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests rank in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently score in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, also show weak to poor performance profiles.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring more RAM than compute power without upgrading to larger, more expensive instance classes. However, the tradeoff is lower compute performance per vCPU due to the older Intel Xeon architecture. It is best suited for memory-sensitive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, small database instances, basic web serving, and lightweight enterprise applications.
